messages.subject: Question about CI value calculation
parts:
Hi all,


Similar to the post here, I am trying to calculate the confidence intervals for a set of Zcr values derived from the ‘compare.Cr’ function. I have looked into the code provided and found that these were calculated using the following code where res.spec and res.hypoth are the results from two iterations of the compare.Cr function (one comparing different species and different modularity hypotheses respectively):


#Species

CI.sp<-qnorm(res.spec$sample.r.sd)/2


#Hypotheses

CI.h<-qnorm(res.hypoth$sample.r.sd)/2; CI.h[1] <- 0



I am wondering if someone would be able to walk me through this calculation- is it based on a specific formula for calculating confidence intervals? More specifically, I am a little lost on what the qnorm function is doing in this context, but would appreciate any general explanation on what this calculation is doing.


Thanks in advance for any help!


Rossy

‘qnorm’ is the quantile function from base-R.  Try:

qnorm(.95)

qnorm(.975)

 

https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/stats/versions/3.6.2/topics/Normal
